title: Нагиев замечает поваров в зале  (Nagiyev Spots the Cooks on the Floor)

segments.t: Spotting Senya, Fedya, and Lyova carrying plates across the dining room floor right in front of the visiting film director, a horrified Nagiyev excuses himself from the table. He pulls Vika and Chef Barinov aside and is outraged to learn that the waitresses never showed up for their shift.
Вы не знаете, где ваши подчиненные?
Знаете, о чем это говорит, а?
Now let's break down each line of their conversation.
'What on earth are the cooks doing in the dining room?' Chef Viktor raises the pitch on 'they do' to turn the phrase into a direct spoken question. Lyova answers right away.
'What is the meaning of this?' The grammar packs 'what' and 'this' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'The cooks are personally bringing out what they prepared.' Chef Viktor brings out the contrast between 'cooks' and 'yourself' in a few short words.
'What the hell are you people doing, huh?' Notice how Russian expresses 'you' and 'and' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'We will fix everything right now.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'we' before landing on 'will fix'.
'So to speak.' The grammar packs 'like this' and 'say' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'Follow me, right now.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'behind' and finishing on 'me'. Lyova answers right away.
'What is going on in our restaurant?' In Russian, the idea of 'and' flows naturally into 'is going on' without extra filler words.
'They did not show up for work today.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'they' before landing on 'today'.
'What do you mean, they did not show up?' In Russian, the idea of 'how' flows naturally into 'came out' without extra filler words. Chef Viktor answers right away.
Вы не знаете, где ваши подчиненные?
'You do not even know where your own subordinates are?' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'you' before landing on 'subordinate'.
Знаете, о чем это говорит, а?
'Do you know what that says about you, huh?' Lyova brings out the contrast between 'know' and 'about' in a few short words.
'And you know, the old man is right.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'and' before landing on 'right'. Now let's put it all back together and hear the whole scene again.
Вы не знаете, где ваши подчиненные?
Знаете, о чем это говорит, а?

That wraps up this scene as stunned to see line cooks serving tables in front of the film director, Nagiyev drags Chef Barinov and Vika aside and learns that none of the waitresses came to work. See you next time!
